questions.q: The French Revolution began in which year?
questions.exp: The French Revolution began in 1789 with the storming of the Bastille on 14 July 1789. It ended the French monarchy and established the First French Republic.

questions.q: World War I started in which year?
questions.exp: World War I started in 1914 following the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand of Austria. It ended in 1918 with the Allied victory.

questions.q: The United Nations was established in?
questions.exp: The United Nations was established on 24 October 1945, after World War II. It replaced the League of Nations and currently has 193 member states.

questions.q: Who was the first man to walk on the Moon?
questions.exp: Neil Armstrong became the first human to walk on the Moon on 21 July 1969 during NASA's Apollo 11 mission. His words: 'One small step for man, one giant leap for mankind.'

questions.q: The Renaissance began in which country?
questions.exp: The Renaissance (meaning 'rebirth') began in Italy in the 14th century. It was a period of cultural, artistic, and intellectual revival that later spread across Europe.

questions.q: The Cold War was primarily between which two countries?
questions.exp: The Cold War (1947–1991) was a geopolitical rivalry between the United States and the Soviet Union (USSR). It ended with the dissolution of the USSR in 1991.

questions.q: The Berlin Wall fell in which year?
questions.exp: The Berlin Wall fell on 9 November 1989. It had divided East and West Berlin since 1961. Its fall symbolized the end of the Cold War and led to German reunification.

questions.q: The American Declaration of Independence was signed in?
questions.exp: The American Declaration of Independence was signed on 4 July 1776. This date is celebrated as Independence Day in the United States.

questions.q: World War II ended in which year?
questions.exp: World War II ended in 1945. Germany surrendered on 8 May 1945 (V-E Day) and Japan surrendered on 2 September 1945 (V-J Day) after atomic bombs were dropped on Hiroshima and Nagasaki.
